title: Dismiss Substack subscribe popups
question: How do I stop Substack's subscribe popup?
answer: Substack has no reader setting to turn off the subscribe popup that covers a newsletter's home page when you are logged out. The usermods script on this page hides that full-screen popup before it draws and shows the newsletter's home page that Substack hides behind it, with scrolling working. Without a script, click "No thanks" under the email box whenever it appears.
prompt: Hide the full-screen subscribe popup on Substack newsletters.
details:
The script injects CSS at page start. It hides `.intro-popup`, the full-screen welcome box with the email field, and undoes what Substack does to the page while that box is open: `overflow: hidden` on `<html>` and `visibility: hidden` on the home page content.

It runs on `*.substack.com` addresses only. Publications on their own domain (for example a newsletter at `www.example.com`) need that domain added as an extra `@match` line. It does not touch the subscribe buttons and boxes inside posts. The check loads one publication's home page logged out.

alternatives.title: Click "No thanks"
alternatives.body: The popup has a "No thanks" link and a close button. Either one closes it and lets the page scroll.

alternatives.title: uBlock Origin filter
alternatives.body:
This hides the popup but leaves a blank page that can't scroll, because Substack also hides the content underneath. Not run by the check.

```
substack.com##.intro-popup
```

evidence.note: Greasy Fork total installs: "Substack: Auto-close the subscribe, referral, and sign-in popups" (7)
